back: A very large market in which most customers buy similar, standardised products.
A small, specialised segment of a larger market with particular needs.
Large sales volume, economies of scale, low prices, risk spread, brand recognition.
Strong (price) competition, high costs of entry and advertising, specific needs unmet.
Less competition, higher prices and margins, customer loyalty, suits small firms, targeted promotion.
Small volume, higher unit costs, depends on one group, attracts larger rivals, limited growth.

front: Which approach suits a small new business?
back: Usually niche marketing: avoids price competition with large firms that have economies of scale.

front: Example of a firm using both approaches?
back: A drinks firm selling a mass-market cola and a niche sugar-free version.
